chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed thirty dinars to free one of our companions, but that amount was not found [in the estate]. He said: 'Buy [a slave] from the people with it and then free him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the money designated for freeing a slave in a will is not found in the estate?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedure for executing a bequest of thirty dinars for manumission when the specific slave is not found in the estate. The ruling emphasizes that the funds are to be used to purchase a slave from the general public (*al-nas*) and free them, ensuring the testator's intent is fulfilled even if the original subject of the bequest is unavailable. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of prioritizing the realization of the deceased's will through flexible application of available assets.
